newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - buoyed by sliding equities.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - buoyed by sliding equities.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds in late trade on Friday recovered to unchanged as traders bet asset allocators would turn to fixed-income markets because the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell sharply, losing 247.37 points.

"Your high-grades were unchanged overall, slightly easier in a few spots (and) secondary activity was light," municipal bond analyst said. "Dollar bonds closed unchanged; the market opened down 1/4 of a point, it was down an 1/8th at noon, and it came back in the late afternoon," he added.

Treasury bonds recently have won back some of their big losses, setting a new range, when measured by yield, of about 6.55 to 6.70 percent, and a trader said that prices might firm further if the stock market continues its slide on Monday.
"Bonds could be bid on as an asset allocation play next week, that's why bonds have a bid," a trader said.

The market appeared fairly confident that the Federal Reserve's policy making arm will make no changes in interest rates when it meets on Tuesday. "The question is what's going on with the dollar and what's going on with the economy," a traders explained.

Early weakness seen in the dollar against the Deutschmark because of fears Germany will raise interest rates as soon as Tuesday spilled over into fixed-income markets, and the dollar/mark was below 1.82 in late trade.
The economic reports next week include housing starts on Tuesday, the trade balance on Wednesday, followed by the Phiadelphia Federal Reserve on Thursday.

In Chicago debt futures, the September municipal contracts closed off two ticks at 119-23/32. The September T-bond contracts settled unchanged at 113-20/32. The MOB spread fell about three ticks from levels seen earlier to plus 195 ticks.
In the secondary market, Denver, Colorado, City & County Airport revenue bonds of 2017, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.45 percent, NET, down two basis points.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of 2027, which carry a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 97-1/2, unchanged.
